session_dialogue.text: Hello. How are you feeling today?
I'm feeling a bit anxious today. I just got a notice about my insurance claim, and it's all a bit overwhelming.
I'm sorry to hear that. It's completely normal to feel overwhelmed when dealing with something like this.
Thanks for understanding. I keep thinking I should have handled it better, but I can't seem to figure out where I went wrong.
It's okay to feel that way. You're not alone in feeling unsure about how to handle things.
I know, but it's so hard not to feel like a failure when I mess up something as simple as managing my own money.
You're not failing—you're just human. Everyone has moments where things don’t go as planned.
I know, but it's hard to convince myself of that when I'm stuck in this loop of self-criticism. I keep thinking I should have known better.
It’s tough when your mind keeps going back to the same thoughts. But you’re doing the best you can, and that’s enough.
I know I’m trying, but it feels like no matter how hard I push, I’m still not good enough. It’s exhausting.
You’re not alone in feeling that way. It’s okay to feel exhausted—what matters is that you’re still showing up, even when it’s hard.
I know I’m showing up, but sometimes it feels like I’m just going through the motions. I don’t know how to stop the guilt from creeping in.
It’s hard to feel like you’re not truly present when guilt keeps pulling you back. But you’re here, and that’s a step forward.
I know I’m here, but it feels like I’m stuck in this cycle of guilt and self-criticism. I don’t know how to break free.
You’re not stuck—you’re just caught in a pattern that’s hard to see clearly right now. And that’s okay. You don’t have to break free all at once.
I wish I could just stop thinking like this. It’s like the guilt is a part of me now, and I can’t seem to shake it.
It’s understandable to feel like the guilt has taken root, but it doesn’t have to define you. You’re allowed to feel this way, and it’s okay to ask for help.
I know I should ask for help, but every time I think about it, I feel like I’m admitting I’m not capable. It’s so frustrating.
You don’t have to be capable in every way to deserve support. Asking for help is a sign of strength, not weakness.
I know you're right, but it still feels like a betrayal of everything I've tried to do on my own. I just want to stop feeling like I'm failing.
